area: F1 Core: modelling DSL, compile, presolve, scaling, MPS/LP I/O, result types

findings.title: MPS and LP readers accept non-finite and out-of-range numbers; the engines then return success statuses with wrong answers
findings.claim: README §2.2 (MPSFormat, LPFormat): a malformed file throws SolverError.invalidModel. README risk 12: malformed inputs yield SolverError.invalidModel. MPSFormat.swift:9-13: values of magnitude 1e20 or more are mapped to ±inf only on the side where an infinite bound makes sense, because read as finite numbers they would poison ratio tests. ModelDiagnostic.nonFiniteValue: NaN, or infinite on the wrong side (compile() enforces this; the readers do not).
findings.observed: MPS: 'UP BND x -1e400' (or '-inf') with row e: x = 0 is read with xl = xu = -inf. Simplex and InteriorPoint both return .optimal with objective -inf at x = [-inf]. 'LO BND x 1e400' gives .optimal with objective +inf at x = [inf]. 'RHS r 1e400' on a G row (min x s.t. x >= 1e400) gives .unbounded. 'RHS COST nan' gives .optimal with objective NaN. 'RHS r nan' gives .optimal. LP: 'x >= 1e400' in Bounds gives .optimal with objective inf. 'r: x >= 1e400' gives .unbounded. 'obj: x + 1e400 y' is read as cost +inf and Simplex returns .optimal with objective NaN. 'r: 1e400 x + y >= 1' makes Simplex return .infeasible, although y = 1 is feasible. Across 28,000 mutated inputs per format, the fuzzer had both readers accept models with row or column bounds of [inf,inf] or [-inf,-inf], c0 = NaN or inf, or non-finite coefficients.
findings.whyWrong: These files should be rejected with invalidModel, as compile() rejects the same values. Instead the solvers return .optimal at a point that violates a row (x = -inf against x = 0), .unbounded for a model bounded below by 1e400, and .infeasible for a feasible model. By consequence this is the critical class (wrong answer with a success status). It is rated high because it takes non-finite or overflowing literals, which only corrupt or untrusted files contain.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/IO/MPSFormat.swift:286 (RHS/RANGES values stored unchecked), :327-328 (bound values: only NaN rejected, ±inf accepted on either side), :403-415 (only xl > xu checked, no row sanity); Sources/ZTronLPCore/IO/LPFormat.swift:335 (Double(...) overflow to inf accepted), :462-465, :655-660
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && for f in up-minus-1e400 lo-1e400 rhs-1e400-G objrhs-nan rhs-nan; do perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 file mps Slots/F1/inputs/$f.mps; done; for f in lp-lo-1e400 lp-rhs-1e400 lp-coef-1e400 lp-rowcoef-1e400; do perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 file lp Slots/F1/inputs/$f.lp; done; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 mps
findings.evidence: up-minus-1e400.mps: read xl=[-inf] xu=[-inf] rl=[0] ru=[0]; Simplex: optimal obj=-inf x=[-inf]; IPM: optimal obj=-inf. rhs-1e400-G.mps: rl=[inf]; Simplex: unbounded; IPM: unbounded. objrhs-nan.mps: c0=nan; Simplex: optimal obj=-nan. lp-rowcoef-1e400.lp: Simplex: infeasible. lp-coef-1e400.lp: c=[1, inf]; Simplex optimal obj=nan.
findings.documented: Not documented. Risk 12 admits there was no fuzzing and predicts traps, not silent acceptance. The MPSFormat doc comment claims that wrong-side huge values stay finite. No test in MPSFormatTests or LPFormatTests feeds NaN, inf or overflowing literals.

findings.title: Presolve.expandBasis returns an optimal-status basis that is dual infeasible and disagrees with the returned duals
findings.claim: README §2.2: postsolve maps 'a solution, a ray or a basis between the reduced and the original problem' (expandBasis). SimplexAnalysis.basis is 'Reusable as WarmStart.basis'. The basis that comes with an .optimal result should be an optimal basis of the original LP and should match the returned duals.
findings.observed: Minimal case: min x s.t. -4x >= 4, x in [-1,1]. With Simplex(.dual) and presolve on, the basis is {x basic, row logical atLower}. The basis's own duals are y = -0.25, so the logical at its lower bound has d = -0.25 and the basis is dual infeasible. The reported duals are y = [0] with d_x = 1 while x is basic. A warm start from this basis takes 1 pivot; the presolve-off basis takes 0. On random LPs: 24 of 540 seeds gave a dual-infeasible basis and 45 of 540 a basis that disagrees with the reported duals. All of them had presolve on, under every engine and scaling. x, y and d themselves always passed KKT.
findings.whyWrong: Take a column fixed by presolve whose reduced cost points at its own original bound. expandDual (sign test, :401) correctly gives the singleton row a zero dual. expandBasis instead treats any .fixed column as resting on the bound the row created, makes it basic and puts the row's logical at a bound. The resulting basis is not optimal and does not match the reported (x, y). Warm starts and the conditioning analysis of the 'optimal basis' (InteriorPoint.finalBasis and Conditioned use the same postsolve) work from the wrong basis.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/Model/Presolve.swift:438-445 (current == .fixed claims the row whichever side the reduced cost points to), compare :401
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 basisrepro ; perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 presolve 60 600 | grep -B1 'dual-infeasible: \["'
findings.evidence: presolve=true: optimal obj=-1.0 x=[-1.0] y=[0.0] d=[1.0, 0.0]; basis status=[basic, atLower]; basis's own duals [-0.25] dual-infeasible [k=1 atLower d=-0.25]; warm start from it: optimal iterations 1. presolve=false: basis [atLower, basic], dual feasible, warm start 0 iterations.
findings.documented: Not documented. PresolveTests.aBasisIsMappedBothWays and postsolveInvariantsHoldOnRandomProblems check only structure (m basics, the round trip through reduceBasis), never optimality or agreement with the duals, so they cannot catch this.

findings.title: CompiledLP.maxViolation(at:) reports zero violation for a point that contains NaN
findings.claim: README risk 1 offers CompiledLP.maxViolation(at:) as the independent check of a point. Its doc comment: 'The largest violation of a column bound and of a row bound at x, both >= 0.'
findings.observed: Bounds [0,1]^2, row 1 <= x0 + x1 <= 2, x = [NaN, 0.5]: maxViolation returns (bounds: 0.0, rows: 0.0).
findings.whyWrong: Every comparison with NaN is false, so Swift.max keeps its earlier argument and the NaN coordinate and NaN row activity vanish. The check that the README recommends for validating a point accepts a meaningless one.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 dsl   (line 'maxViolation flags a NaN point')
findings.evidence: FAIL | maxViolation flags a NaN point | (bounds: 0.0, rows: 0.0)

findings.title: An infeasible or tolerance-level conflicting one-variable constraint makes compile and solve throw invalidModel instead of returning .infeasible
findings.claim: README §2.1 presents CompileOptions.lowerSingletonConstraints ('a one-variable constraint becomes a bound; on by default') as a choice of representation. SolveStatus.infeasible: 'The model has no feasible point.'
findings.observed: minimize x + y s.t. x <= -1 (x >= 0 from its domain), x + y >= 0: Simplex().solve(model) throws 'invalid model: variable x has lower bound 0.0 above upper bound -1.0'. With lowerSingletonConstraints = false the same model returns .infeasible. 'x >= 1 + 1e-12' together with 'x <= 1' also throws, although presolve would treat a 1e-12 crossing as a fixed column.
findings.whyWrong: An infeasible LP is not an invalid model, and the outcome flips with an option documented as representational. The diagnostic blames bounds the user never wrote. Bounds that cross by rounding noise are a hard error, with no tolerance applied.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/Model/Compile.swift:209-227 (singletons tighten bounds, then guard xl[j] <= xu[j] throws with no tolerance)
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 dsl   (INFO lines 'infeasible singleton')
findings.evidence: INFO | infeasible singleton x <= -1 (x>=0): solve threw invalid model: variable x has lower bound 0.0 above upper bound -1.0 / same model with lowerSingletonConstraints=false: status infeasible / singleton x>=1+1e-12 and x<=1: solve threw invalid model
findings.documented: Partly. The compile() doc lists 'lower > upper on a variable' among the errors it throws. Neither README nor HANDBOOK says that an infeasible one-variable constraint becomes an error rather than an .infeasible status.

findings.title: Solution.dual(ofConstraintNamed:) double counts when two named one-variable constraints imply the same bound
findings.claim: Analysis.swift:155-160: a lowered constraint 'receives the reduced cost when the bound it implies is the active one'. The presolve's own postsolve handles the same situation ('the last and tightest claims the reduced cost and the others see none left').
findings.observed: min x + y s.t. a: x >= 2, b: 2x >= 4, c: x + y >= 1 gives ya = 1, yb = 0.5, yc = 0, so ya + 2*yb = 2 != c_x = 1. Kept as rows, the same model gives duals [1, 0, 0].
findings.whyWrong: Each lowered constraint independently claims the whole reduced cost, so the reported duals are not a valid dual solution (the stationarity residual is -1).
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 misc
findings.evidence: FAIL | ... | ya=1.0 yb=0.5 yc=0.0: c_x - (ya + 2yb + yc) = -1.0; INFO | same model as rows: duals [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

findings.title: The free-format MPS round trip is not bit-exact for range rows
findings.claim: MPSFormat.swift:3-5: the writer emits shortest round-trip numbers 'so read(write(lp)) == lp'. Test name: rangeRowsReadBackBitForBit.
findings.observed: 15 of 400 random models read back different, only in range-row bounds, by at most 2.2e-16 relative to the larger end. Examples: rl -388213.4614957075 -> -388213.4614957074; -5.323138532990446e-11 -> -5.3231197227887606e-11; -2.0 -> -1.9999999999999996. Every other field, including adversarial names, survives exactly.
findings.whyWrong: When the 8-ulp search for an exact R fails, the writer falls back to R = hi - lo, and lo is then not reproduced. The equality claim is false, although the numerical effect is about one ulp of the larger bound.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 roundtrip 0 400 | grep MPSDIFF
findings.evidence: round trip seeds 0..<400: MPS exact failures 15 ... MPSDIFF seed 4 onlyRangeRows=true maxErrRelToLargerEnd=1.52e-16
findings.documented: Not documented. The writer doc claims an exact round trip.

findings.title: The MPS writer produces a file its own reader rejects when a constraint is named ""
findings.claim: MPSFormat.write doc: free format 'keeps every name ... so the output round-trips'. The DSL accepts .named("").
findings.observed: LPModel.minimizing(x + y).subjectTo { (x + y >= 1).named("") }.mpsString() writes ' G ' in ROWS and '    x  1.0' in COLUMNS. MPSFormat.read then fails with 'line 4: a ROWS line needs a type and a name'. The LP export of the same model reads back.
findings.whyWrong: The writer's 'usable' check rejects the empty name, but the replacement it substitutes is still empty.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 emptyname
findings.evidence: FAIL | MPS export of a constraint named "" reads back | invalid model: line 4: a ROWS line needs a type and a name

findings.title: LP export drops columns that have no cost, no row and default bounds, and renumbers columns; README describes only the Rg column
findings.claim: README §4 'Not verified': LP and MPS exports round-trip through this package's own readers. README §4 'File formats' names only the Rg column as a change made by LP export.
findings.observed: Columns [a, b, c], where a has no cost or row, read back as [b, c]. Columns [a, b, c], where c has no cost or row, read back as [b, a]. Column indices, and so positional solution vectors, do not survive.
findings.whyWrong: The README presents the LP round trip as structure-preserving apart from the Rg column. Only the test helper's comments acknowledge the dropped column and the renumbering.
findings.location: Sources/ZTronLPCore/IO/LPFormat.swift:32 (only nonzero costs written), :66-76 (default bounds not written)
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 lp   (INFO lines 'LP round trip')
findings.evidence: INFO | LP round trip (a has no cost/row): columns [a, b, c] -> [b, c]; (c has no cost/row): [a, b, c] -> [b, a]
findings.documented: Only in the comments of Tests/ZTronLPCoreTests/LPFormatTests.swift:12-13 and :38, not in README or HANDBOOK.

findings.title: .unbounded Simplex results carry an objectiveValue although hasSolution is false
findings.claim: SolutionAnalysis.objectiveValue: 'nil without a primal solution'. SolveStatus.hasSolution: 'True when a primal solution accompanies the status', which is false for .unbounded.
findings.observed: min -x - y s.t. x - y <= 1, x, y >= 0 gives .unbounded with hasSolution = false and objectiveValue = -1.0, with presolve on and off.
findings.whyWrong: The two doc comments together promise nil here. A caller that reads objectiveValue without checking the status gets the objective of an arbitrary last iterate.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 unbobj
findings.documented: README risk 9 documents the last iterate in primal for unbounded results, but says nothing about objectiveValue.

findings.title: The LP writer can emit duplicate row labels, and the LP reader accepts duplicate row names
findings.claim: LPFormat.write keeps row names apart from the generated Rg columns, and names are uniqued. compile() and the MPS reader both reject duplicate row names.
findings.observed: Rows [a (range), a_] with a column named Rga: row a is renamed a_ and collides with the existing row a_, so both are written as 'a_:'. LPFormat.read returns rows [a_, a_] without error; the optimum is preserved.
findings.whyWrong: The writer appends '_' without re-checking uniqueness, and the reader does not reject duplicate labels, so a name lookup on the result is ambiguous.
findings.repro: cd /Users/admin/Documents/ZTronLPOptimizer/verification/probes/cycle-A && swift build --product F1 -c release && perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' 120 .build/release/F1 misc2
findings.evidence: LP text: ' a_: x + Rga - Rga_ = 0' and ' a_: x + z <= 3.0'; read back: rows [a_, a_]

summary: Cycle A, finder F1 (core). The most important claims held under independent oracles: DSL semantics, compile, the Solution API, presolve/postsolve with scaling across 18 engine configurations on 600 random LPs and 13 netlib instances (KKT checked on the original problem), integer presolve by enumeration, MPS/LP section and bound semantics, round trips, and 56,000 fuzzed files with no trap or hang. Ten findings. The most severe (A1-01, high, critical-class consequence): both readers accept non-finite or overflowing numbers (1e400, inf, nan) on the wrong side, and the engines then answer .optimal with x=-inf, .optimal with objective NaN, a false .unbounded or a false .infeasible, against README's promise of invalidModel. Medium: Presolve.expandBasis can return a dual-infeasible basis that disagrees with the returned duals (about 4% of random LPs; tests check only structure); maxViolation(at:) passes NaN points; an infeasible one-variable constraint throws invalidModel instead of returning .infeasible. Low: double-counted duals of duplicate lowered constraints, range rows not bit-exact in the MPS round trip, an empty name breaking the MPS export, undocumented LP column dropping and renumbering, objectiveValue on .unbounded, duplicate LP row labels.
